earlier_scan.source_named: Retired ISO code (2008): Garreh-Ajuran is a pair of ethnic groups speaking Borana or Somali, not a distinct language (Glottolog bookkeeping entry)

sources.citation: Held source folders for the two real languages: bora1271 (Borana Oromo: Hodson & Walker 1922; Owens 1985 Harar excerpt; Appleyard 1991; Gamta 1999) and soma1255 (Somali: Biber 1982; Downing & Nilsson 2019; Green 2022; Andrzejewski 1956 abstract) -- of each read to confirm coverage
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not re-examined for this item; noted only to show that the varieties the Garreh and Ajuran actually speak are covered under their own glottocodes (soma1255 already in catalog; bora1271 in the target list with held sources).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request Number 2007-172: retire [ggh] Garreh-Ajuran, merged into Borana [gax] and Somali [som] (submitted 2007-08-01 by John Ommani, Bible Translation and Literacy, Nairobi; adopted 2008-01-14). 8 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; it is an administrative form. Sec. 3(c) p. 2: 'Garreh-Ajuran is not a specific language, but rather a pair of closely allied ethnic groups. The Garreh people speak Borana as a first language and Somali as a second language while the Ajuran people are divided into two groups; those who speak Borana as a first language and those who speak Somali as a first language.' Sole source cited (p. 4): 'BTL's sociolinguistics survey among the Garreh, Ajuran and Sakuye people' (unpublished).

Nothing. Page states the code was 'Split between Borana [gax] and Somali [som]' per change request 2007-172, effective 2008-01-14; no descriptive references listed (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.note: The standard first-hand account of Booran noun accent (ultimate vs penultimate by gender, per Appleyard 1991); relevant to what Garreh speakers actually speak. Belongs under bora1271.

sources.citation: Andrzejewski, B. W. 1957. Some preliminary observations on the Borana dialect of Galla. Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies 19(2): 354-374.

sources.note: Primary description of the Borana (Kenya/southern Ethiopia) variety that the Garreh and part of the Ajuran speak; already on the bora1271 list of works to obtain. Listed here only as a pointer; the item should be handled under bora1271.

sources.citation: Bible Translation and Literacy (BTL), Nairobi. c. 2007. Sociolinguistic survey among the Garreh, Ajuran and Sakuye people (unpublished report cited as the sole source in ISO 639-3 change request 2007-172).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only document on record specifically about the Garreh/Ajuran speech situation; would settle which Borana/Somali dialects the groups speak, but as a sociolinguistic survey it is unlikely to contain a stress statement.
